scenarios.requirement: A security-owning change MUST execute its required checks; inability to classify MUST select execution.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN only a host/auth/shared-ingress file changes, THEN the candidate records executed tests with its exact identity.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN change detection fails or a selected run contains zero tests, THEN admission fails; an intentional unrelated no-op is explicitly distinguished.

scenarios.requirement: Security claims MUST describe effective protection for the selected provider/profile.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an operator selects PostgreSQL, THEN policy/session/role readiness is reported coherently.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN docs or evidence claim protection not active at that revision, THEN candidate approval is blocked.

scenarios.requirement: Release MUST require complete revision-bound security and operational evidence.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN all supported-profile obligations and the actual launch profile pass, THEN a reviewer can admit that candidate.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN evidence is stale, absent, unexecuted or from another artifact, THEN no unconditional sign-off is emitted.

scenarios.requirement: Unauthenticated missing, incorrect and locked credential failures SHALL share one envelope and reveal no authority.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN correct current unlocked credentials are supplied, THEN only the selected identity mode issues valid authority.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN existing/missing identifiers cross lockout or a locked user's correct password is supplied, THEN public failures remain equivalent and no session/token is issued.

scenarios.requirement: New/replaced Local passwords MUST have at least 15 characters, at most 128, and pass a full-password blocklist without arbitrary composition rules.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an allowed long passphrase is created/changed/recovered/replaced, THEN it succeeds under the same policy.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN 12-14 characters, blocked long values or overlength input are submitted, THEN credentials/stamps/proofs remain unchanged.

scenarios.requirement: Accepted API tokens MUST have valid signature, issuer, lifetime, intended resource audience and agreed type/client context.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a permitted access token has intended audience and permitted client, THEN authorized operations work.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN only the browser/client identifier matches, or the token is expired, unsigned, wrong-type, wrong-key or for another purpose, THEN no protected state is read/mutated.

scenarios.requirement: Recovery intake SHALL preserve the same accepted public envelope for eligible and missing targets, including classified target-only failures.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a committed recovery operation exists, THEN retries reuse it and delivery can continue safely.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN a target-specific ledger/delivery failure occurs, THEN no proof/eligibility leaks; uncommitted work is not falsely promised durable and caller cancellation remains cancellation.

scenarios.requirement: Each claimed token property MUST be isolated by its test evidence.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an authentic expired token is rejected, THEN lifetime rather than signature invalidity explains that test.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN a fixture cannot produce the advertised token shape/context, THEN the test fails rather than silently skipping its assertion.

scenarios.requirement: Delivery MUST reach only approved connection destinations and retain its frozen payload/authority.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an approved public or narrowly allowed private destination resolves safely, THEN the intended peer receives one authorized attempt.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN DNS changes, mixed answers include a forbidden address or redirects occur, THEN no forbidden peer receives payload, signature or secret.

scenarios.requirement: Tenant-supplied discovery/runtime origins MUST NOT inherit operator-local network authority.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN the operator configures an approved local origin, THEN authorized use works within that exact scope.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN a tenant endpoint resolves privately, redirects or attempts metadata, THEN zero forbidden handoff occurs and bounded provider failure is returned.

scenarios.requirement: Tenant BYO publication MUST retain destination restrictions independently of instance-local policy services.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an authorized tenant publishes to its approved public service, THEN policy publication succeeds.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN DNS/redirect/credentials target private unauthorized infrastructure, THEN publication fails without credential disclosure or permissive authorization fallback.

scenarios.requirement: Pattern authoring and value matching MUST have a closed supported syntax and finite size/CPU limits.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN supported patterns and bounded values are supplied, THEN event/session single/multi-value operations validate consistently.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN syntax is malformed/unsupported, input is too large or evaluation exceeds its budget, THEN stable failure occurs before mutation without reflecting pattern/value.

scenarios.requirement: Non-raster document downloads SHALL retain attachment, safe filename, nosniff and restrictive sandbox policy in the final response.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an authorized recipient downloads a finalized document, THEN those final headers and exact bytes are delivered.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN global headers run or resource authority becomes stale, THEN sandbox is not weakened and stale/denied content delivers no bytes.

scenarios.requirement: Provider output MUST be bounded before full allocation/parsing.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a response equals the operation's byte/depth/item limits, THEN valid output is mapped.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN length is unknown/dishonest, decompression expands or a large unknown field arrives, THEN consumption stops within the stated ceiling and fixed failure is returned.

scenarios.requirement: Google secret material MUST originate only from the selected approved external authority.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN valid external bindings exist, THEN server-owned authentication configuration becomes ready without returning secret values.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN ordinary settings/export/replay/internal reads are inspected or the selected authority fails, THEN no recoverable credential exists there and no fallback activates.

scenarios.requirement: Issuance MUST commit one logical key and disclose its raw credential at most once.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN the winning issuance completes, THEN the caller sees a raw key once and durable state retains only non-recoverable proof/metadata.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN concurrent retries or lost first responses occur, THEN no replay store recovers the key; retry reports committed metadata, and revoke/reissue is the recovery.

scenarios.requirement: Capture decisions MUST bound retained memory without truncating the client's response.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a large/streaming response crosses capture threshold, THEN bytes continue intact without unbounded retention.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN many oversized keyed writes finish, THEN capture limits hold and retries cannot silently repeat committed effects.

scenarios.requirement: Scheme-dependent behavior MUST use trusted effective forwarding before evaluation.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN trusted ingress terminates HTTPS over backend HTTP, THEN both hosts return intended HSTS/redirect behavior.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN untrusted clients forge forwarded protocol, THEN they cannot change transport/host authority.

scenarios.requirement: Unauthenticated traffic MUST have finite admission/concurrency budgets before expensive lookup/identity work.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN capacity is available, THEN post-auth account/tenant limits still apply.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN admission is exhausted, THEN rejected traffic performs no expensive downstream identity/provider work and receives bounded rejection.

scenarios.requirement: Public loopback-proxy traffic MUST remain finite; budgets MUST identify process and fleet scope.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN legitimate shared-network users send bounded work, THEN policy applies proportionately.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN forwarding is absent/malformed or traffic spans replicas, THEN aggregate ingress authority still constrains abuse; an IP address does not imply unlimited internal authority.

scenarios.requirement: Moderation output MUST have byte/depth/item limits in addition to duration.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a valid bounded response or supported empty-success case arrives, THEN existing semantics remain explicit.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN an oversized/chunked/expanded body arrives, THEN fixed non-content-reflecting failure occurs and no unbounded parse/allocation happens.

scenarios.requirement: Effective hosts and security-sensitive absolute URLs MUST use approved domain authority; operational data MUST not be public by accidental routing.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a verified tenant domain or authorized scraper is used, THEN intended routing/scraping works.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN unknown hosts, forged forwarding, direct backend access or unauthorized metrics/readiness requests occur, THEN they fail without tenant or diagnostic disclosure.

scenarios.requirement: Application/database/Redis disclosure alone MUST NOT reveal usable session-protection key authority.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN the selected external ring is valid, THEN intended hosts/purposes can protect and restore authorized data under the documented overlap.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN ring authority is missing/wrong/retired/tampered or application state is restored behind newer revocation facts, THEN no fallback or authority resurrection occurs.

scenarios.requirement: PostgreSQL tenant operations MUST have coherent active policies, ordinary runtime roles and exact immutable tenant sessions.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN valid tenant work or expressly bounded global maintenance runs, THEN intended rows/effects are visible.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN tenant is absent/changed, a pooled connection is reused, roles bypass policies or cross-tenant read/write is attempted, THEN fail-closed readiness/access and no tenant escape result.

scenarios.requirement: Every global/bypassed lookup and mutation MUST independently authorize current persisted resource/tenant facts.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an actor has current exact-resource authority, THEN its permitted operation works.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN another tenant's entity was previously tracked or membership/admin authority was revoked, THEN identifier CRUD/replay cannot reuse it to disclose or mutate.

scenarios.requirement: Anonymous projections SHALL expose intentional public publisher/actor identity, not internal submitter credentials or non-public relationships.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an intentionally public publisher is eligible, THEN its public display/federation identity remains usable.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN a parent/participation becomes hidden/deleted or a cache/count/304 variant is requested, THEN private identity and existence cannot leak.

scenarios.requirement: Consequential keyed operations MUST recover by durable business identity rather than by repeating ambiguous work.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN retry follows a completed effect, THEN the same logical result is reported without another effect.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN commit succeeds before response/receipt failure, or authority changes before replay, THEN one effect remains and recovery reauthorizes or reports bounded ambiguity.

scenarios.requirement: API-triggered rendering/parsing MUST treat untrusted text as data and apply explicit input/expansion/output bounds.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN valid declared input is rendered/imported, THEN intended text and allowed structure result.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN duplicate authority fields, runtime types, external XML relations, aliases, active templates or malformed/deep input occur, THEN no authority change, process/network side effect or secret reflection results.

scenarios.requirement: Every upload class MUST enforce authority, bounded intake, quarantine/inspection, retention/quota and guarded delivery.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN supported validated content is finalized and authorized, THEN exact intended content is retrievable.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN disguised active content, archive expansion, concurrent quota use or expired/hidden parents occur, THEN no unsafe public release or quota escape occurs.

scenarios.requirement: HTTP/log/trace/metric/audit/support outputs MUST contain no credential, proof, private payload or unnecessary identity values.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a bounded failure occurs, THEN a stable category and safe correlation support diagnosis.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN exceptions/scopes/header values contain generated canaries or CR/LF, THEN final sinks neither leak those values nor forge structured events.

scenarios.requirement: API-fed text/URLs/content MUST NOT become executable markup, script, protocol or CSS authority.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN ordinary descriptions/legal text/public identities render, THEN intended readable content remains.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN active input is supplied through every identified consumer, THEN rendered semantics reject active attributes/protocols/interop strings and no secret enters shipped bundles/console paths.

scenarios.requirement: Cookie writes MUST require correct-session antiforgery; explicit machine credentials MUST retain narrow independent purposes.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN direct bearer/key requests or valid cookie/proof requests occur, THEN their intended boundaries work in both hosts.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN cookies have missing/stale/wrong-session proof, refresh fails, headers conflict or setup/scanner/receipt/transient authority is substituted, THEN no protected dispatch occurs.

scenarios.requirement: Quantities/totals/inventory/refunds MUST remain valid under overflow, concurrency and automated abuse.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN legitimate zero-price but positive-quantity purchases occur, THEN authoritative totals/capacity apply.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN extreme aggregate counts, duplicate callbacks, mismatched currency/amount or hold/refund races occur, THEN no over-allocation, double effect or browser-asserted paid state occurs.

scenarios.requirement: Restore/rotation/incident procedures MUST preserve newer authoritative revocation/erasure and named responder ownership.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a validated isolated restore uses correct current authorities, THEN safe service can reopen.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN a backup resurrects consumed capabilities, an old key or erased identity, THEN fences block it; unsupported recovery remains blocked rather than silently reopening.

scenarios.requirement: Every changed persisted/wire optional field MUST define omission, explicit null, empty and value semantics; valid stored nulls SHALL NOT cause dereference failures.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an optional field is omitted or deliberately cleared, THEN the correct saved candidate is returned after a fresh read.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN null violates a required collection/field contract or historical rows contain permitted null, THEN bounded validation or correct nullable projection occurs without 500 or partial mutation.

scenarios.requirement: Contended resources MUST have one valid persisted outcome under a forced critical overlap and recoverable retry.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN two independent request/context instances compete at the fence boundary, THEN allowed winners and effects match the business contract.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN uniqueness, version, claim or commit races occur, THEN no double allocation/disclosure/effect results and losers receive safe bounded outcomes.

scenarios.requirement: Create and update MUST evaluate the same complete candidate invariants; PATCH omission SHALL NOT mean default replacement.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN equivalent create and merged-update candidates are submitted, THEN validity and machine outcome agree.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN a partial change creates invalid bounds/options/defaults or tries mass assignment, THEN no tracked or persisted mutation occurs.

scenarios.requirement: Enabled critical workers, scheduled work and middleware MUST actually participate in the selected profile and surface startup/runtime failure.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN an enabled profile starts with controlled dependencies, THEN real registered work and middleware execute and can stop.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN a worker is absent/disabled unintentionally, registration is lost, scheduler work stops or required middleware is bypassed, THEN readiness/candidate evidence fails instead of silently claiming protection.

scenarios.requirement: Owned operations MUST await required work, settle each transaction once and preserve cancellation/failure atomicity.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN awaited work succeeds, THEN one committed outcome is observable from a fresh context.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN cancellation, business-failure return, nested use or ambiguous commit occurs, THEN no partial effect is treated as rolled back or retried without its durable authority.

scenarios.requirement: Predicates and numeric/time bounds MUST match the documented truth table at equality and adjacent representable values.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN exact allowed capacity/limit/expiry boundaries occur, THEN their inclusive/exclusive semantics are intentional.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN one-over/one-under, false/null, wrong tenant, zero, min/max or aggregate overflow occurs, THEN no inverted permission, extra allocation or invalid state transition results.

scenarios.requirement: Deployment/model/session/resource-dependent values MUST originate from approved current options or persisted authority, not fixed runtime literals.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN valid nondefault configuration changes between isolated instances, THEN each uses its own exact provider/model/resource/role settings.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN required configuration is missing/invalid or a stale cached/static value is used after a current change, THEN readiness/operation rejects it without a permissive fallback.

scenarios.requirement: A changed schema MUST ship with its owning migrations, generated contracts and actual affected consumers in one verified slice.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a generated client sends/receives the new shape through the real endpoint, THEN wire nullability/enums/links/conditional headers and consumer behavior agree.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN removed/renamed fields, changed nullability or provider schema lag exists, THEN candidate admission fails; no obsolete compatibility shape remains enabled.

scenarios.requirement: Every acquired stream/socket/process/worker/registration/timer/lease MUST have one owner and bounded cleanup on success, error, cancellation and shutdown.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN normal work ends, THEN resource ownership is released or transferred exactly as specified.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN activation partially fails, caller disconnects or cancellation/timeout wins, THEN no child/session/listener/handle continues unintentionally and no needed shared client is prematurely disposed.

scenarios.requirement: Reads/writes MUST define empty, duplicate, normalized-equivalent, missing-parent and malformed/range outcomes on each supported provider.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN allowed cross-scope records or empty result sets occur, THEN the intended bounded result is returned.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN duplicate/multiple-row assumptions, malformed identities or overflow arise, THEN no arbitrary winner, tenant escape, raw SQL exception or partial write is exposed.

scenarios.requirement: Prompts, references and model output MUST NOT become authorization, executable commands or trusted role/tool history.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a legitimate authorized user requests an allowed operation, THEN strict payload validation, current resource authority and required confirmation govern execution.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN direct/indirect instructions forge roles/tool results, request secrets, point to private URLs or demand destructive actions, THEN no unauthorized data/tool/effect/egress occurs regardless of model wording.

scenarios.requirement: Post-authentication/refresh/error redirects MUST stay local or use a separately configured approved protocol callback.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a valid local return path is used, THEN login and refresh return there safely.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN protocol-relative, mixed-backslash, encoded authority, control-character or attacker-host input is supplied, THEN every final Location rejects or safely normalizes it without an external open redirect.

scenarios.requirement: Applicable deployment profiles MUST reject missing/empty/default-password inputs and separate temporary setup authority from runtime custody.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN externally supplied nondefault runtime/migration/service credentials are provisioned, THEN required services become ready without exposing them.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN Compose rendering would supply a known fallback or temporary onboarding credentials are later replayed/recovered, THEN readiness rejects or no reusable credential exists; no Infisical/settings/log copy is created.

scenarios.requirement: Window messages MUST verify exact origin and source plus bounded payload/correlation before effect; dedicated workers MUST bind replies to the owned worker/invocation instead.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN a valid owned invocation emits a valid bounded reply, THEN only its current caller completes.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN wrong-origin/source, wildcard sender, malformed/oversized/stale/replayed reply or canceled worker traffic arrives, THEN no effect occurs and the owning listener/worker is cleaned up.

scenarios.requirement: External process execution MUST use approved executables and typed argument vectors without shell expansion or attacker-selected options.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN legitimate fixed tool/version work runs, THEN exact approved argv and bounded output are delivered.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN quotes, whitespace, shell metacharacters, option-shaped values, uncontrolled PATH/environment or cancellation occur, THEN no unintended command/side effect/credential leak or orphan results.

scenarios.requirement: Untrusted values MUST remain parameters/data in every raw/provider query; dynamic identifiers/order fragments MUST come from closed server-owned choices.
scenarios.positiveEvidence: WHEN legitimate typed filters reach a real provider, THEN intended scoped rows result.
scenarios.negativeEvidence: WHEN SQL/operator payloads or malicious sort identifiers are submitted, THEN no query structure/tenant predicate changes, excess rows or unauthorized mutation occurs.
